# NBA Analytics Web App — Feature Survey

**Stack:** Next.js 14 (App Router) + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS, with a static-JSON data layer generated by an R analytics pipeline (`run_full_pipeline.R`, `build_*.R` scripts). No database or server API — all pages are statically rendered from precomputed JSON files in `web/public/data/`.

---

## 1. What it is

A single-page-app-style dashboard that presents the outputs of a Monte Carlo NBA season simulation (1,000 simulated seasons, 4 model variants/engines, ~1.23M simulated games) plus a growing set of secondary analytics modules (coaching impact, shot charts, offseason transactions, player projections, model diagnostics). The R pipeline does all the modeling/statistics offline; the Next.js app is purely a presentation and exploration layer over the resulting JSON exports.

## 2. Navigation / Feature Map

Routes are defined in `web/components/Sidebar.tsx` and `web/app/*`:

| Route | Feature | Core Idea |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | **Season Standings** | Win-distribution visualizer + full standings table for all 30 teams, toggleable in one tab (`StandingsClient.tsx`). Shows simulated win totals, playoff odds, etc. |
| `/offseason` | **Offseason Moves** | 2026–27 trade/free-agency/draft analysis: team-by-team roster deltas, transaction log, draft prospect profiles, projected win-trajectory impact (`OffseasonClient.tsx`). |
| `/variants` | **Model Variants** | Side-by-side comparison of the 4 underlying simulation engines (Bottom-Up BPM, Bayesian RAPM, Shot Quality & Fatigue, 16-D Embeddings) and their divergence/ensemble blend (`VariantsClient.tsx`). |
| `/players` | **Player Projections** | ~330-player pool with projected games/MPG/points/rebounds/assists and statistical outlier badges (`|z| > 2.0`) (`PlayersClient.tsx`). |
| `/shots` | **Shot Charts** | Per-player shot charts with empirical-Bayes-smoothed hot-zone detection and binomial z-score significance testing (`ShotsExplorerClient.tsx`, `PlayerShotChart.tsx`, `ShotChartModal.tsx`, `InlinePlayerShotCard.tsx`). |
| `/coaches` | **Coaching Staffs** | Coaching-impact analytics decoupling tactics from roster talent: ATO (after-timeout) efficiency, challenge/game-theory decisions, talent-adjusted win lift, 5-D coach radar profiles, waterfall talent→wins bridge (`CoachesClient.tsx`, `CoachRadarProfile.tsx`, `AtoEfficiencyScatter.tsx`, `CoachImpactWaterfall.tsx`). |
| `/diagnostics` | **Diagnostics** | Model-accuracy transparency: reliability/calibration curves, Brier score (currently 0.2284), accuracy drift over time, residual distributions (`DiagnosticsClient.tsx`, `BrierScoreComparison.tsx`). |
| `/teams` | Redirect shim | Forwards to `/?tab=table` (legacy link compatibility). |

A persistent sidebar (desktop) / drawer (mobile) in `Sidebar.tsx` provides navigation plus a small "Simulation Spec" info card (Monte Carlo sim count, total games, margin-σ explainer popover, variant count) and a footer status indicator ("Pipeline Active", version tag).

## 3. Underlying analytical sophistication

This isn't just a stats display — the R pipeline implements genuinely advanced methodology, surfaced through the UI:
- Monte Carlo season simulation with a logistic/normal win-probability model (`P(Win) = Φ(margin / σ)`, σ ≈ 11.8 pts), run across 4 independently-weighted model variants and blended into an ensemble.
- Empirical Bayes shrinkage + binomial z-tests for shot-zone "hot zone" significance (avoids small-sample noise in shot charts).
- Coaching-impact isolation using talent-adjusted residuals (actual vs. expected NetRtg), ATO points-per-possession, leverage-weighted coach's-challenge success, and (per the implementation plan) Double Machine Learning / synthetic controls for confounder-adjusted win lift.
- Explicit model calibration reporting (Brier score, reliability curves) rather than just raw predictions — a transparency feature uncommon in fan-facing NBA sites.

## 4. Intended audience

- **Primary:** the author/analyst themself and a technically literate audience (data-savvy NBA fans, sports-analytics hobbyists, fantasy/betting analysts) who want simulation-grade probabilistic projections rather than simple point-estimate stats.
- **Secondary:** a portfolio/demonstration audience — the UI's methodology call-outs (Brier scores, σ explainer popovers, "ADR-I Frozen Reference Compliant" badge, named model variants) read as deliberately showcasing rigor, suggesting this doubles as a technical portfolio piece (e.g., for data-science/analytics job applications) as much as a fan tool.
- Not aimed at casual fans — there's no plain-language "who will win the title" framing; everything is expressed in statistical/modeling terms (z-scores, σ, Brier, RAPM, DML).

## 5. What makes it unique

- **Multi-engine transparency:** most fan projection sites show one black-box number; this explicitly exposes 4 differently-specified models and their disagreement/ensemble blend as a first-class feature (`/variants`).
- **Self-grading:** the `/diagnostics` page holds the model accountable with calibration curves and Brier scores against historical outcomes — most hobbyist projection tools never publish how wrong they've been.
- **Coaching as a quantified, talent-independent signal:** `/coaches` tries to econometrically strip out roster quality to isolate coaching-specific value (ATO execution, challenge decisions, rotation entropy) — a niche not covered by mainstream sites like ESPN or basketball-reference.
- **Full offseason transaction modeling:** treats trades/FA/draft as inputs to a quantitative win-trajectory re-simulation rather than static roster lists.
- **Statistically rigorous shot charts:** empirical Bayes + binomial z-testing for zone significance, instead of raw FG% heatmaps.
- **Fully static, pipeline-driven architecture:** no backend/API — an R pipeline produces versioned JSON artifacts consumed by a static Next.js build, making the whole thing reproducible and cheap to deploy.

## 6. Current state notes

- `/coaches`, `/offseason`, and `/shots` are newly scaffolded (untracked files per git status) and backed by a detailed implementation plan (`COACHING_ANALYTICS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`) describing a 5-phase build (data ingestion → R analytical engine → Next.js presentation → QA). Some of this work appears in-progress rather than fully wired end-to-end.
- Styling is a consistent dark "slate/indigo/amber" theme throughout (Tailwind), with a seasonal Halloween basketball logo currently in the brand mark.
